The paper proposes KEEP, a prompt-learning framework for CLIP-style vision-language models in image classification. It uses retrieval augmented generation to obtain knowledge for prompts, and it runs experiments on eight datasets.

The question is whether this is multimodal-only RAG (E9). The task is image classification with a VLM, and the knowledge is image-wise, so the setting is clearly multimodal. Text-only RAG is in scope, but this is not text-only. It does mention RAG, but the generator is a VLM or foundation model working on images.

It is not clearly a language model conditioning on retrieved text, because the retrieval is likely image-based with domain foundation models such as BiomedCLIP. The retrieved knowledge then feeds into prompt learning. That is ambiguous, but E9 fits better than INCLUDE, since the abstract says "various image modalities" and the setting is vision-language. I considered MAYBE because the RAG component might be text-based, with an LLM generating knowledge. Still, the whole system is multimodal, so I lean toward E9.

{"decision": "EXCLUDE", "code": "E9", "reason": "Multimodal VLM/CLIP image classification prompting; RAG used in vision-language setting, not text-only."}
